AWPTCM-T33250.objective:
• A VLAN configured with arp-mac-disparity accepts ARP replies that map a unicast IP address to a virtual multicast MAC address (NLB cluster).
  • A VLAN configured with arp-mac-disparity unicast accepts ARP replies using a virtual unicast MAC address for an NLB cluster.
  • Static ARP entries can be configured with a unicast IP address and multicast MAC address and bound to specific ports.
  • The arp-mac-disparity configuration (including multicast, unicast, and multicast-igmp modes) persists in the running and startup configuration and survives stack failover.
  • When arp-mac-disparity is enabled with appropriate mode and port binding, traffic to the virtual NLB address is forwarded only to the configured ports instead of being flooded across the VLAN.
  • arp-mac-disparity operates correctly when the relevant VLAN interface belongs to a VRF instance.
  • Disparate ARP entries are correctly reflected in show arp and platform MAC/IP tables.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Configure a VLAN with arp-mac-disparity (or multicast mode). Send an ARP reply using a virtual multicast MAC for a unicast IP. Verify the disparate ARP entry is learned and visible in show arp.
Configure arp-mac-disparity unicast on a VLAN. Send a virtual unicast MAC ARP reply and confirm the entry is learned and traffic is handled appropriately.
Configure a static ARP entry using unicast IP + multicast MAC bound to specific ports. Verify the binding and that mac-address-table reflects the entry on the configured ports.
Save the arp-mac-disparity configuration (with mode) to startup-config. Perform a reload or VCS failover. Confirm the configuration and disparate ARP behaviour are restored.
With arp-mac-disparity and static ARP binding configured, send traffic to the virtual IP/MAC. Confirm forwarding occurs only to the bound ports (no VLAN-wide flooding).
Configure the NLB server VLAN inside a VRF instance with arp-mac-disparity. Verify the feature functions (ARP learning and forwarding) within the VRF.
Verify that show arp, show platform table macaddr, and related commands accurately report the disparate ARP entries, virtual MACs, and port bindings.
Disable arp-mac-disparity (or change modes). Confirm that subsequent virtual MC ARP replies are dropped or handled according to default behaviour.
